reason: Algae at the living coast could provide a starting point for life spreading onto wet ground.
expectation: Coastal algae will begin a transition toward life on land.

effect: Algae at the coast became shore plants, establishing a starting point for life on land.
reaction: The new challenges of moisture and exposure make the transition clear.
reason: Weathered rock could provide a surface for shore plants to colonize, without assuming soil already exists.
expectation: The plants and weathered rock may begin forming a substrate for further land life.

alternatives.reason: Checking their partners would clarify the route if this guess is wrong.

effect: Shore plants and weathered rock made soil, providing a substrate for further land growth.
reaction: The distinction between wet rock and soil is clear and satisfying.
reason: Shore plants and soil are a plausible next step toward clothing the wet ground.
expectation: The plants will spread over the soil, creating more established land vegetation.

effect: Shore plants in soil produced roots, suggesting a foundation for taller land plants.
reaction: The connection between underground support and height is satisfying.
reason: Roots may help shore plants grow into more established vegetation.
expectation: Rooted plants will develop further on land.

alternatives.reason: Checking partners could clarify what roots enable.

effect: Roots combined automatically with light to make ferns, suggesting a path toward taller vegetation.
reaction: The compatibility hint clarified the route after my wrong guess.
reason: Ferns and soil are a plausible way to establish vegetation across the ground.
expectation: Ferns will spread over the soil and help clothe the wet ground.

alternatives.reason: Checking partners would avoid another guess.

effect: Ferns have no available combinations, so they are not the next ingredient.
reaction: I was surprised the ferns could not be used further.
reason: Inspecting soil may reveal how to establish ground cover or continue toward a forest.
expectation: The report will show any available partners for soil, possibly advancing land vegetation.

effect: Soil has no available combinations, so it does not currently suggest the next step.
reaction: The lack of soil partners leaves the route unclear.
reason: Shore plants may have another available partner for clothing the wet ground.
expectation: The inspection will reveal whether shore plants can advance either goal.

effect: Shore plants and air produced windblown spores, opening a route for plants to spread.
reaction: The distinction between spores and seeds clarified what this dispersal achieves.
reason: Inspecting the new spores should reveal where they can spread and may advance the ground-cover goal.
expectation: The spores will have a partner that helps establish new growth.

effect: Spores and soil produced moss, completing the wet-ground goal; the forest remains.
reaction: The spores-to-moss route makes the spread onto wet ground clear.
reason: The remaining route to a forest is unclear, so inspecting moss may reveal a useful partner.
expectation: Moss may have a partner that advances land vegetation toward a forest.

effect: Moss and water formed a wetland, adding a habitat but leaving the forest goal unfinished.
reaction: The waterlogged soil's lack of air is an interesting consequence.
reason: The wetland is the newest development, and its role in making a forest is unclear.
expectation: The inspection may reveal a partner that continues the route toward a forest.

effect: Wetland and ferns made the first forest, completing the remaining goal. The passage makes clear that this is a compressed, branching history, not moss turning into trees.
reaction: The forest was satisfying to reach, especially with that evolutionary caveat.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making soil from shore plants and weathered rock was most worthwhile: it gave the spread of land life a physical foundation without treating wet rock as fertile soil.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying ferns with soil and then inspecting soil was frustrating: neither offered a way forward at that point.

surprise.text: I was surprised that ferns initially had no available combinations, then became usable once the wetland existed.

arbitrary.text: Roots combining with light to produce ferns was not obvious to me; I relied on compatibility feedback after trying shore plants instead. The result explained the role of light and roots, though.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what the forest enables next; the chapter made habitats and plant adaptations interesting while acknowledging the limits of its compressed history.
